candidate.selection_reason: executes zip with file list from user-controlled directory -> potential command injection via filenames
candidate.source_summary: File paths come from grain directory mounted at /tmp/tmp/data via bind mount from user-provided grainDir parameter. Files are enumerated recursively from the current directory (which is /tmp after pivot_root) using listDirectory().
candidate.sink_summary: zip command executed with -@ flag reads file list from stdin. File paths are written directly to zip's stdin via pipe without shell escaping.
candidate.guard_summary: findFilesToZip function filters out files containing newlines to prevent command injection via filename newline characters. Sandbox environment isolates the process with namespace and mount restrictions.
candidate.risk_pattern: User-controlled file paths from grain directory are passed to zip command via stdin without proper escaping beyond newline filtering, potentially allowing zip command injection through specially crafted filenames.
called_function_context: findFilesToZip() recursively processes files and filters newlines
enclosing_conditions: if (!restore) branch - only in backup mode, not restore mode
candidate.context_summary: The zip command is executed in a sandboxed environment with file paths coming from user-controlled grain directory. While newlines are filtered to prevent basic injection, other special characters in filenames may still affect zip command behavior.
unresolved_facts: Whether zip command properly handles other special characters in filenames beyond newlines
Whether the sandbox environment fully prevents escape or privilege escalation
What specific zip command-line parsing vulnerabilities might exist with the -@ flag

target_cwe.description: The product constructs all or part of an OS command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended OS command when it is sent to a downstream component. This weakness can lead to a vulnerability in environments in which the attacker does not have direct access to the operating sy...
target_cwe.impact: code execution, data access, data modification
remediation_steps: Use parameterized queries and prepared statements
Implement strict input validation with whitelisting
